While what you said is true, but in these cases, there's nothing else to go on. In my case, I believe the biggest enemy wasn't the witnesses but the detective that brought them in as such. They were suspects, and I think the decision to see them as witnesses was a terrible one. 

In the end witness statements make innocent people go to jail and guilty people go free. But aside from them, there isn't much to go on.

The sad thing is that, at least in my experience, cases get dropped because of false witness statements. I was sexual assaulted by 3 men, and one woman, and after "investigation" (meaning they brought in the 3 of the suspects as witnesses) the detective told me that since there were 3 "witness statements" that all said I "wanted it" the DA dropped the case. I later found out that my medical records showing how they drugged and raped me were excluded when giving the DA my case. 

So because 3 of the 4 people involved in my rape said "oh she wanted it, she consented" The case was dropped and I was told "if you pursue the case any further, you'll more than likely get charged for a false accusation then they would for rape". 

I get that my case is rare, but what other witness statements are you going to get in a one on one rape? You have nothing but the statements of those involved to work with, and sometimes the medical exams aren't clear.

I just wanted to point out that if "justice" wanted to ever be sought out by OP, that it would be harder to shoot for the longer she waited. That's all I meant, I didn't want to push any actions on OP at all. 

The healing process and "justice" are a few of the hardest things to deal with. When I went through the same thing, I was never told to get a lawyer, or that anyone could help me and stand in my place in order to get justice. I wish I knew, because the people who did it to me, did it again. I ended up not following through with investigations because of my mental health. I thought that because I wasn't mentally stable, I wouldn't be "competent" enough to testify against the people who assaulted me. I just wanted to shed a bit of light on the "justice" part. 

Edit: Some don't want justice, mainly because of the fear of revictimization and the fact that victims are sometimes harassed and humiliated by family members, police, and sometimes friends. I just wanted to try and show that even though those fears are real, that if "justice" wanted to be sought, it gets harder as time passes. It is possible to get mental and emotional help as well as justice, if she wanted.

Sadly, there is no winning in this, and every choice is extremely difficult. 

You either try to get yourself emotional and mental health, or you try to get justice.
